b: For the average American, the military is a better option than college. If you are able-bodied, and have no connections to a career, the military is almost always a better option than college.

In college, you’re making a gamble, taking on student loan debt in the hopes there’s a better paying job on the horizon. Some of us have friends and family that can help get us a foot in the door for that first job. However, the majority of us have to fight tooth and nail to acquire these positions. In today’s world, making connections is way more valuable than busting our asses for degrees. As cliche as it sounds, “It’s not what you know, it’s who you know.” There are way too many college degree holders working dead end jobs now. I saw only about 30% of degree holders are working in their field! Why are we paying thousands and thousands of dollars for a useless piece of paper? What a scam.

Don’t get me wrong, the military isn’t all roses and daisies. You have to leave the comfort of your own home, go through the grueling process of basic training, then go to tech school. Once you make it through these challenging tasks, the world is your oyster. You’re guaranteed a military job in whatever you trained in! What college program can do that? You’re given benefits, PTO, you can work anywhere in the world! Not to mention you get the GI bill. Free college! You can get a degree, while acquiring some real-world work experience, and make connections in the military to prepare you for life after service. And yes, there’s always the possibility you would get sent out to war, but there is only a very small percentage of service members that ever see combat. A very small trade-off for all the benefits you’re receiving.
I don’t think this applies to everybody, but I think in today’s AI-driven cutthroat economy, the military would be more beneficial for the vast majority of us than college.
